question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Mercantilist Colony / Trading Post — European Power That Controlled It]
options: Batavia (Jakarta) — Dutch East India Company (VOC) headquarters in Southeast Asia
New Amsterdam (New York) — Originally a Dutch colonial settlement before passing to the English in 1664
Pondicherry — Major French trading post on the Coromandel Coast of India
Goa — Established as a Portuguese base on the Malabar Coast of India on the western coast
wrong_fact: Goa is located on the Konkan Coast (sometimes called the western coast of the Deccan), NOT the Malabar Coast. The Malabar Coast refers specifically to the southwestern coastal region of present-day Kerala. Goa is further north, in present-day Goa state.
explanation: Goa was captured by Alfonso de Albuquerque in 1510 from the Bijapur Sultanate. It lies on the Konkan/western coast of India (in today's Goa state), clearly distinct from the Malabar Coast (Kerala). The other three options are correctly matched: Batavia was indeed the VOC headquarters; New Amsterdam was the Dutch settlement that became New York; Pondicherry (Puducherry) was the main French base on the Coromandel Coast.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Mercantilist Trade Concept / Route — Correct Geographical or Economic Association]
options: Triangular Trade — Connected Europe, West Africa (slaves), and the Americas in a trade circuit
Balance of Trade — Mercantile policy of ensuring exports exceed imports to accumulate bullion (gold/silver)
Cape Route — Portuguese-controlled sea route from Europe around the Cape of Good Hope to Asia, bypassing the Ottoman-controlled Levant
Levant Trade — European overland and sea trade with South America via the Mediterranean, bypassing the Ottoman Empire
wrong_fact: The Levant refers to the eastern Mediterranean region (modern Syria, Lebanon, Israel/Palestine, and Turkey) — NOT South America. Levant Trade was the established commerce between Europe and the Near East / Asia (spices, silk) passing through Ottoman-controlled eastern Mediterranean ports like Alexandria and Beirut. It had nothing to do with South America.
explanation: The Levant is the eastern Mediterranean coastal region. 'Levant Trade' refers to the lucrative commerce in spices, silk, and other Asian goods that passed through Ottoman-controlled eastern Mediterranean ports, prompting Europeans to seek alternative sea routes. South America was not involved in the Levant trade at all. The other three options are correctly matched: the Triangular Trade circuit, Balance of Trade doctrine, and the Cape Route's role in bypassing Ottoman territory are all accurately described.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Mercantilist European Power — Primary Geographical Focus / Region of Economic Exploitation]
options: Spain — Americas (Caribbean, Mexico, Peru); extraction of silver from mines at Potosí (Bolivia) and Zacatecas (Mexico)
Portugal — African and Asian coasts; control of sea trade from Lisbon via the Cape Route to India, Malacca, and Macau
England — North American Atlantic seaboard, Caribbean; Mercantile Acts enforced trade within a closed imperial economic system
France — Primarily focused mercantilist extraction on the East African Coast and the island of Madagascar as its main colonial revenue base
wrong_fact: France's primary mercantilist focus was NOT primarily East Africa or Madagascar. France concentrated on North America (New France: Quebec, Louisiana, the Great Lakes region), the Caribbean (Saint-Domingue/Haiti, Martinique, Guadeloupe — highly lucrative sugar colonies), and India (Pondicherry, Chandernagore). East Africa and Madagascar were relatively minor and late additions to French interests.
explanation: French mercantilism was centred on its sugar-producing Caribbean colonies (especially Saint-Domingue, the most profitable colony in the 18th century), New France in North America, and its Indian trading posts (Pondicherry, Chandernagore, Masulipatnam). While France did have interests in Madagascar, it was never the primary mercantilist revenue base. The other options are correctly matched: Spain's silver from Potosí and Zacatecas, Portugal's Cape Route and Asian trade empire, and England's Navigation Acts are all accurately described.
